Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our senior editors. America is a scientific superpower and a wellspring of new products, techniques and business models. But does it rank at the top of the innovation league table? And has President Donald Trump hurt or helped its standing? His administration has championed cutting-edge industries like semiconductors, fintech and artificial intelligence (“Whoever wins AI, WINS!”). But he has also attacked the country’s leading universities, restricted skilled immigration and cut funding to public institutions like the National Science Foundation. The Global Innovation Index ranks countries around the world based on a variety of indicators, from patents and venture-capital deals to scientific publications and school test scores. The latest index, published by the World Intellectual Property Organisation, draws partly on data from Mr Trump’s first year back in office. Has America climbed up or tumbled down the league table? And which countries are breathing down its neck? You can find out by reading the full story. Dear professionals, we are pleased to share the September edition of the PFI Monthly Research Report. This issue explores key themes shaping global macro, financial markets, Czech M&A, private equity, banking and real estate — with a common thread running through it: as central banks stop "looking through" inflation, the diversification and valuation assumptions built into portfolios are being tested. In this issue of PFI Monthly you will find: Global macro – Why three major central banks (ECB, Fed, BoJ) tightened within eight days as they grew less willing to look through an energy-driven inflation shock, and what that means for stock-bond correlations; plus a six-factor fundamental framework — interest-rate differentials, inflation expectations, growth dynamics, the current account, NIIP and fiscal credibility — for analysing exchange rates. Financial markets – A contribution analysis decomposing the S&P 500's 1,031% rally since the 2009 low into revenue growth, margin expansion and multiple expansion, with revenue growth likely the only sustainable driver ahead; why longer-dated US Treasury yields at multi-decade highs are a warning equities are not yet pricing; and a study of why temperament, not intelligence, separates good investors from bad. Czech M&A – CVC's minority (~30%) investment in Prague-based CDN77 via its Strategic Opportunities platform, at a reported USD 1.9–2bn valuation — the largest PE deal in CEE technology this year. Private equity – How European hostels moved from a specialist niche to an institutional asset class, with Brookfield, Apollo, King Street and others deploying billions into a fragmented, consolidating market. Banking – The "fintech free-rider" debate: as branches close and neobanks like Revolut scale, should fintechs help fund the physical infrastructure the system still depends on? Real estate – Why the risk premium on privately held CRE has compressed to near cyclical lows, leaving little margin for disappointment if bond yields stay elevated. This edition also includes an interview with Ondrej Konak, Co-Founder of NAVCalc, on building a fund-administration platform from scratch, earning client trust in critical processes, and freeing investment professionals from manual work. 👉 Read the full edition to explore all insights in detail. **Welcome back!** OpenAI put 722 math papers written by a secret model on GitHub. The Pentagon says it has finally stopped using Claude. TIME read the instructions behind Meta's Muse and found it keeps hourly files on you and everyone you mention. And Claude now edits your Google Docs without Claude on Chrome.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** What did a secret model prove in 722 papers?

* **Pentagon:** Why did it take months to pull Claude out of the military?

* **Meta:** What does Muse write down about you every hour?

* **Claude:** Can Claude edit your Google Docs without breaking them?


----------







----------
## OpenAI dropped 722 AI-written math papers on GitHub

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fe886b36-59f7-435a-8eb0-bbf61f1e5df8/Oct_7_-_1.jpg?t=1791363746)
Caption: 

On Tuesday night, OpenAI [put 722 math papers on GitHub](https://github.com/openai/math). A secret model it hasn't released wrote all of them. No human is listed as an author on any of them.

Math is full of open problems, questions nobody has answered, some for over a century. OpenAI handed its model about 4,000 of them and gave each one around three hours of thinking. The answers it kept became 722 papers, grouped into 372 results.

**Some of the claims:**

* You can't color every point on an endless sheet of paper with five colors so that no two points an inch apart match. Open since 1950.

* Catalan's constant, a number people have studied since the 1800s, can't be written as a fraction.

* Progress on the Riemann hypothesis, the most famous unsolved problem in math, without solving it.

Many papers come with proofs a computer can check line by line. Many don't, and OpenAI says some of those could have mistakes.

The nine mathematicians OpenAI consults, including Fields Medalists, asked labs last week to stop testing their models on open problems. This week they said their role is not an endorsement. 

Terence Tao, one of the best mathematicians alive, says problems are being harvested faster than the field can absorb them.

Same night, OpenAI's Codex lead shipped four upgrades and the math proofs on day two of the 28-day promise, put it to a vote, and people still demanded a reset. He gave it.

80382.subject: Did AmEx and Perplexity just launch an AI CFO for small businesses? 🤖📊; Stripe bought its way into lending on pa…
80382.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1135

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Wednesday! Today, we're diving into AmEx & Perplexity's new AI CFO for small businesses to see what it tells us about who will own the AI CFO for SMEs (what Perplexity gets from AmEx's small-business cardholders, why AmEx kept the agent read-only and the payment side in-house, how the package stacks up against Anthropic's Claude for Small Business [ https://substack.com/redirect/56da82ac-b242-4243-9cbe-f0df70a896d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & Meta's Muse [ https://substack.com/redirect/36de4fe5-bf00-47cb-8a1c-0062d53147af?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and what’s next + bonus deep dive into a16z’s State of Markets 2026: The AI Playbook for Founders and Investors [ https://substack.com/redirect/9b2cce3e-4bd9-4d68-bd0c-75c5f547a622?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and breaking down Stripe’s deal to buy Parafin, the lender behind DoorDash, Gusto, Amazon & Walmart Marketplace’s small-business credit (why Parafin’s processor-agnostic model is both what Stripe is paying for & the asset most at risk, why the combined lending business still funds only ~$2B a year next to Square’s ~$7B, & what to watch next + bonus deep dives into Stripe [ https://substack.com/redirect/a458f8f8-8291-4045-aebc-745168eb07f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and Sequoia’s Private AI Briefing, or Why AGI Is Already Here [ https://substack.com/redirect/89bf8678-6713-4b5d-bdf2-64f329b4fac1?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s just jump straight into the interesting stuff 🌶️
Did AmEx and Perplexity just launch an AI CFO for small businesses? 🤖📊
The news 🗞️ Partly. Late last week, finance giant American Express $AXP  and Perplexity launched AI CFO tools for U.S. small businesses: about 10 Skills inside Perplexity Computer [ https://substack.com/redirect/eaf0c52c-80a7-4d0d-9731-53e208cd4b83?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] that turn Amex Small Business Card data into cash-flow forecasts, reconciliation, and tax-season prep. The AI CFO (if we can really call it like that) can now forecast a company’s cash but cannot pay a single bill, and that limit looks quite deliberate.
Because whoever holds payment authority will capture most of the value of AI CFOs for SMEs, and the terms of this deal show AmEx is clearly keeping that authority for itself. 
Let’s take a closer look at this to see what Perplexity gains from a card issuer’s distribution, why AmEx limited the agent to read-only data, how the package compares with Anthropic’s Claude for Small Business [ https://substack.com/redirect/56da82ac-b242-4243-9cbe-f0df70a896d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] and Meta’s Muse [ https://substack.com/re

Novinárčina patrí medzi profesie, pri ktorých výsledok práce okamžite vstupuje do verejného priestoru. Článok, rozhovor, video či reel zasahujú v priebehu niekoľkých hodín zasiahnuť desaťtisíce alebo státisíce ľudí, otvoriť diskusiu, vysvetliť komplikovanú tému alebo priniesť informáciu, ktorá dovtedy verejne nezaznela. S takýmto dosahom človek dokáže otvoriť témy, diskusie a poukázať na dôležité témy. zodpovednosť. Za každým titulkom, číslom, citátom či použitým zdrojom je rozhodnutie konkrétneho človeka a práve séria týchto rozhodnutí určuje, či výsledkom bude len ďalší obsah na internete alebo kvalitná novinárska práca. Dobrý novinár nezačína písaním Písanie je iba jedna časť práce, ale ešte pred prvou vetou treba vyhodnotiť, či téma stojí za pozornosť, nájsť jej najsilnejší uhol, overiť informácie a pochopiť, čo z nich je pre čitateľa skutočne dôležité. Redakciou Startitup každý deň prechádza veľké množstvo správ, dát, vyjadrení, zahraničných tém, tipov či tlačových správ. Redaktor sa v nich musí vedieť orientovať a rozpoznať, čo je len informačný šum a kde sa naopak skrýva téma, ktorá môže mať dosah na veľkú časť Slovenska. Niekedy je podstatný nový údaj, inokedy zmena, ktorá sa dotkne každodenného života ľudí alebo výrok, ktorý si zaslúži bližšie vysvetlenie. Práve schopnosť nezobrať prvú dostupnú informáciu ako konečnú odpoveď patrí k veciam, ktoré odlišujú dobrého novinára od človeka, ktorý iba spracúva obsah. Kontakty sú jedna z najväčších hodnôt tejto profesie Aj keď sa v dnešnej dobe dá veľa vecí spraviť za monitorom, kvalitná žurnalistika si vyžaduje oveľa viac. Tému často posunie ďalej telefonát s odborníkom, človekom priamo z daného prostredia alebo zdrojom, ktorý dokáže informáciu potvrdiť, spochybniť či doplniť o detail, ku ktorému sa iní ešte nedostali. Sieť kontaktov si novinár buduje postupne a jej hodnota nespočíva v počte uložených telefónnych čísel. Dôležitá je dôvera, ktorú si musí zaslúžiť korektnou prácou, znalosťou témy a tým, že s informáciami narába profesionálne. Práve skúsenosť časom mení aj spôsob práce. Novinár už nepozná len fakty, ale vie, komu zavolať, kde môže hľadať ďalšiu vrstvu príbehu a kedy odpoveď, ktorá na prvý pohľad vyzerá uspokojivo, ešte nestačí. Dosah je privilégium aj záväzok Online médium dáva autorovi veľmi rýchlu spätnú väzbu. Krátko po publikovaní vidno, ko
